1003: Section 1003 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the civil rights policies of the Georgia Department of Human Services, Division of Family and Children Services. It includes compliance with nondiscrimination laws such as Title VI, the ADA, and Section 504, prohibiting discrimination based on race, color, national origin, age, sex, and disability in administration of programs, including SNAP. Key forms and processes include the DFCS Civil Rights, ADA/Section 504 Complaint Process and various forms for reasonable modifications and communication assistance (e.g., Form 101 and Form 724). This section specifies training requirements for compliance, such as DHS 1100, to be completed within 30 days and annually. It does not address employment or sexual harassment issues, which are covered in DHS OHR Policies 101 and 102. Caseworker questions related to policy compliance, discrimination complaint procedures, and required public notifications can be answered here, but questions about specific program eligibility should refer to other sections like SNAP Policy 3025 or TANF Policy 1003.
1004: Section 1004 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the nondiscrimination policy related to individuals with disabilities within the Division of Family and Children Services (DFCS). It specifies that no qualified individual with a disability shall be excluded from participation in or denied benefits of services, programs, or activities offered by DFCS due to their disability. The policy applies to all DFCS and Georgia Department of Human Services staff, including volunteers, interns, subrecipients, contractors, grantees, agents, and service providers involved with DFCS's Office of Family Independence (OFI). It excludes child welfare and employment-related matters. There are specific requirements for DFCS to make reasonable modifications to avoid discrimination unless such changes fundamentally alter services or programs. Caseworkers should refer to this section for guidance on disability-related nondiscrimination matters but should consult other sections for child welfare (see Section XYZ) or employment concerns (see Section ABC). There are no specific forms, thresholds, or time limits mentioned in this section.
1008: Section 1008 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines requirements under the National Voter Registration Act of 1993 (NVRA) for voter registration opportunities for individuals applying for or receiving public assistance. It mandates the distribution of a Voter Registration Application form to Food Stamp (FS), Medicaid (MA), and Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) clients at key touchpoints such as application, recertification/renewal, and change of address. The section references specific legal codes, including 52 U.S.C. § 20501 and O.C.G.A. § 21-2-222. This section does not address the procedural details of voter registration, which may belong under Georgia law on voter registration processes. Caseworkers can use this section to understand the distribution requirements of voter registration materials but should refer to other sections for eligibility criteria for FS, MA, and TANF benefits.
2009: This section of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines eligibility and certification periods for immigrants under the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2009, specifically focusing on Iraqi and Afghan immigrants. Key topics include the eight-month eligibility period for applicants with special immigrant status and verification procedures through the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) program. Important forms and charts include CHART 3320.4 and CHART 33, which detail eligibility periods and application dates for Iraqi and Afghan immigrants. Notably, the section emphasizes scenarios where income and resources for ineligible aliens are budgeted differently (refer to sections 3635 and 3630). This section specifically addresses caseworker inquiries about how to verify immigrant status and process their certification under the specified acts but does not cover SNAP budgeting rules for households without immigrants, which are located in different sections.
3000: Section 3000 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual provides an overview of policies relevant to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) following its renaming in the 2008 Farm Bill. This section covers policies on confidentiality, mandating that case information be restricted to certain individuals, as well as voter registration procedures mandated in DFCS offices since January 1995. It also details the mandated reporting procedures for suspected child abuse and outlines nondiscrimination requirements under the Americans with Disabilities Act. Additionally, Title VI and methods for verification when determining eligibility are included. This section does not address specific eligibility criteria, which are found in Section 4000. Caseworkers can use this section to understand information sharing rules, voter registration responsibilities, and how to report child abuse, but will need to refer to other sections for specific eligibility requirements and benefit calculation methods.
3005: Section 3005 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on confidentiality requirements regarding information about food stamp applicants and recipients (A/R). It specifies that such information is restricted to purposes directly connected with the administration of the Food Stamp Program (FSP) and other means-tested federal or state assistance programs. Key rules include the release of information without an A/R's consent in scenarios like investigations or emergencies, with strict documentation requirements. The policy outlines scenarios where confidential information cannot be released to an A/R, such as information obtained through IRS/BEER matches or pending criminal prosecutions. Caseworkers can reference this section for guidance on the legal release of information but should look to Appendix B for policies about hearings (Section 3005 does not cover hearing procedures). It emphasizes that requests for information from unauthorized sources require A/R's written consent. Instances involving inter-agency or legislative requests without meeting required purposes fall under different guidelines outside this section.
3010: Section 3010 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the procedures and requirements for voter registration within the SNAP program. The section details the integration of Voter Registration Information into core application and renewal forms, such as Forms 297, 298, and 508, and emphasizes the disposal of previous form versions. It outlines the responsibilities of caseworkers to read Voter Registration Information to applicants and document responses in Gateway; however, caseworkers cannot influence applicants' political preferences or imply that voter registration affects benefit eligibility. The section mandates monthly reporting of voter registration data and details confidentiality protections for applicant information. Notably, inquiries regarding the status of voter registration applications and assistance with voter registration must be directed to the Georgia Secretary of State Office. This section does not address issues related to determining SNAP benefit levels or processing benefit appeals; those aspects are discussed in other sections of the manual.
3020: Section 3020 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the mandated reporting of child abuse or neglect. It outlines the procedure for making a Child Protective Services (CPS) referral, which includes calling the appropriate county's CPS, documenting the call in Gateway, and maintaining records in the Document Imaging System. Key decision points include whether to maintain the reporter's anonymity and notifying the DFCS Legal Services Office if contacted by the Office of the Child Advocate. Notably, this section does not cover scenarios where abuse occurs in settings unrelated to child protection services (refer to Section 3015 for institutional settings). Caseworkers can refer to this section for guidance on making CPS referrals and understanding their duty to report, but it does not address procedures for other types of reporting or legal counsel during investigations.
3025: The Georgia SNAP Policy Manual Section 3025 provides comprehensive guidelines regarding compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act. The policy addresses specific topics, including qualifications for individuals with disabilities, reasonable modifications, auxiliary aids and services, and procedures for public notifications and complaints. Key forms include the Reasonable Modification and Communication Assistance Request Form (Form 101) and the Request Tracking Form (Form 102). The section explicitly states conditions under which modifications can be denied due to fundamental alterations or undue burdens, with only the Division Director having the authority to make such decisions. This section does not cover nondiscrimination complaints based on race or color, which are addressed in MAN 3700 (DFCS Civil Rights Policy). Caseworkers can refer to this section for guidance on making accommodations for disabilities but not for handling grievances unrelated to ADA or Section 504, such as racial discrimination.
3030: The Georgia SNAP Policy Manual's Section 3030 focuses on Civil Rights compliance, outlining rules prohibiting discrimination in DHS/DFCS programs based on race, color, age, sex, disability, national origin, or other protected classes. It details the requirement for reasonable modifications and auxiliary aids, and specifies the complaint process for civil rights violations, including ADA/Section 504 complaints. Key forms include the DFCS Civil Rights, ADA/Section 504 Complaint Form 724 and the Reasonable Modification Request Form 101. This section is specific to program administration and service delivery and excludes employment and sexual harassment issues, which are covered in DHS OHR Policies 101 and 102. Caseworkers can reference this section for guidance on nondiscrimination practices and complaint processes but must consult other sections for employment discrimination or harassment concerns.
3035: Section 3035 on Verification within the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines comprehensive procedures and requirements for verifying eligibility and benefits for SNAP applicants. It covers critical topics such as the mandatory verification of identity, income (both earned and unearned), citizenship/alien status, residency, student status, and utility expenses. Key forms mentioned include Form 173 (Verification Checklist), and systems like Truv and SteadyIQ for income verification. Specific thresholds, such as changes in unearned income over $100, and time limits like the 10-day period for providing verification, are emphasized. This section also details the use of third-party verification methods, including collateral contacts and computer matches, while addressing conditions for accepting the AU’s statement as a last resort. It indicates scenarios not addressed here, such as details around citizenship/alien status and work registration, which are covered in Sections 3320 and 3350 respectively. This section assists caseworkers in deciding what documentation is required for various eligibility points, clarifying questionable information, and the necessary actions if the required verification isn't provided. However, it does not address the specifics of handling non-eligible members or in-depth immigration criteria, which are covered elsewhere.
3040: Section 3040 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the compliance requirements with the Health Information Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) of 1996, including privacy and security rules for Protected Health Information (PHI). It specifies that DHS employees, volunteers, trainees, and contractors must adhere to HIPAA regulations, utilizing only the minimum necessary PHI for specific purposes. Key forms include Form 5460, Notice of Privacy Practices, required at each application for assistance. Notable exceptions where authorization is not required involve TPO, public health, and certain legal situations; however, third-party disclosures and non-health-related uses do require authorization. This section cannot answer questions related to non-HIPAA confidentiality requirements found in other sections.
3100: Section 3100 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the application process for SNAP benefits, starting from the request for benefits to notifying the Assistance Unit (AU) of eligibility. Key requirements include verifying citizenship, immigration status, and Social Security Number (SSN) for applicants, while non-applicants are exempt from these verifications, though their income and resources are assessed. The section mandates that applications can be requested through multiple channels and requires timely processing, with a screening for expedited processing. It references legal bases such as the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 and certain Social Security regulations. Caseworkers can use this section to understand application submission protocols and verification requirements but should refer to Section 3205 for detailed definitions of an Assistance Unit and to other sections for procedures involving changes after the application process.
3105: Section 3105 covers the full application processing workflow for SNAP: right to same-day filing, interview scheduling, Notice of Missed Interview (NOMI), agency/client delay tracking, verification requirements, benefit proration from application date, and certification period assignment. Chart 3105.1 and 3105.2 detail certification periods. Critically, Chart 3105.3 'Disposition of SNAP Applications' governs what happens to expedited-service applications where verification was postponed: if the household returns with verification within 60 days, the case is reactivated (no new application needed) and benefits are prorated from the date verification is provided. Questions about reactivating a postponed-verification application after the household returns belong here via Chart 3105.3. NOT HERE IF: the question is about the 7-day expedited SOP deadline or initial expedited screening — those belong in §3110. NOT HERE IF: the question is about verification types or sources — see §3035.
3110: Section 3110 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the expedited application processing for SNAP benefits, detailing the conditions under which an Assistance Unit (AU) is eligible for expedited services. To qualify, an AU must meet specific criteria such as having less than $150 in monthly gross countable income and liquid resources not exceeding $100, or having higher monthly shelter and utility expenses than their income and resources. The section specifies that applications must be processed by the 7th day following the application date, necessitating timely screening using the expedited screening tool (Form 296). Notable stipulations include the verification of identity as the sole requirement before benefits issuance. The section includes protocols for SNAP Employment and Training (E&T) referrals using Gateway Form 864. Scenarios involving destitute migrant workers are covered, but detailed procedures for ABAWD and NAC matches direct readers to Sections 3355 and 3380. Caseworker queries about verification, E&T compliance, and processing timeframes can be addressed, but issues regarding work exemptions or time limits for ABAWDs are outside this section's scope.
3115: Section 3115 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses special considerations for processing SNAP applications. It discusses the procedure for Assistance Units (AUs) where all members are applying for or receiving SSI, allowing them to apply for SNAP at the Social Security Administration (SSA) office, without the requirement of an in-person interview. The section outlines joint TANF/SNAP or General Assistance (GA)/SNAP application procedures and includes Chart 3115.1 for processing SNAP applications filed at SSA offices. Key decision points include the determination of the application date when received by mail, expedited processing eligibility, and conditions for processing applications without contacting applicants. Notable exceptions include cases where incomplete applications require follow-up. This section provides guidance on processing SNAP applications in specific scenarios, but does not address unrelated issues like resource limits covered in Section 3120 or income calculations found in Section 3130.
3120: Section 3120 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the rules and procedures for designating an Authorized Representative (AR) for SNAP benefits. Key topics include the responsibilities an AR may undertake, such as filing applications, attending interviews, and managing benefits during the certification period. It specifies the necessity of written documentation or a release form from the Assistance Unit (AU) to designate an AR. Important decision points include the disqualification criteria for an AR who misuses benefits, the notification process for disqualification, and the AU's right to appeal such actions. This section also addresses exceptions for drug and alcohol treatment centers (refer to Section 3220) and stipulates additional verification steps for ARs who represent multiple assistance units. Caseworkers can use this section to understand AR responsibilities, documentation requirements, and disqualification procedures but should refer to Section 3220 when dealing with treatment centers or migration-specific policies.
3125: Section 3125 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual covers the Disaster Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (DSNAP), specifically highlighting eligibility criteria, income and resource considerations, and application procedures. The policy defines eligibility based on residence or work location during a disaster, with income limits and specific conditions such as adverse effects from the disaster. Important forms include the DSNAP Application for Benefits (Form 854), and key timeframes relate to the benefit period beginning at the disaster date and a three-day processing standard of promptness (SOP). Income limits and maximum monthly allotments are detailed in a chart for various household sizes. The section emphasizes scenarios not applicable to DSNAP, such as Citizenship/Alien Status, which are addressed elsewhere (e.g., Section 3120). It answers caseworker questions about eligibility determination and application processing but does not address regular SNAP program rules or citizenship criteria.
3200: Section 3200 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual details the formation and requirements of Assistance Units (AUs). Key topics include defining the individuals who comprise an AU, determining the AU size as it relates to income limits, and utilizing the income and resources of AU members to assess eligibility. Notably, income and resources of individuals not included in the AU but financially responsible can still affect eligibility. The section does not cover specific threshold numbers or forms, which are likely detailed in Sections 4100 and 4200. It also does not address joint custody or shared household scenarios — see Section 3300 for those. Caseworkers find guidance here on how to compose an AU and what financial data is necessary, but it does not address income calculations or timeframe requirements directly.
3205: Section 3205 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on the formation and determination of SNAP Assistance Units (AUs). It outlines specific criteria for AU composition, including individuals who live together and purchase/prepare meals jointly, and addresses exceptions for separate AU status. The section identifies key decision points, such as the inclusion of spouses and children under parental control, and exclusion criteria for individuals who face disqualifications or sanctions. Important resources and instructions include Chart 3205.1 for AU composition, verification sources, and criteria for special AU members like boarders and institutional care residents. For residents of institutional or group settings (shelters, group homes, transitional housing), §3205 still governs the core AU composition question: specifically, whether residents who receive more than 50% of their meals from the facility must be treated as a separate one-person AU rather than part of the household. This communal meal / 50% meal rule is applied here even when the facility-specific rules live in §3215-3230. This section assists caseworkers in determining AU composition, eligibility, and the inclusion of specific individuals but does not cover budgeting specifics, which are found in section 3600.
3210: Section 3210 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses categorical eligibility for specific household types, including seasonal farm workers, strikers, students, and Teen Parent Improvement Program (TPI) residents. It outlines criteria such as alignment with TANF Community Outreach Services (TCOS) for households with income levels below specified Federal Poverty Levels (FPL) and the conditions that disqualify a household from categorical eligibility, such as containing an IPV disqualified member or exceeding income limits. Eligibility establishment hinges on applicant signatures on key forms like Form 297, Form 297A, or the SNAP/Medicaid/TANF Renewal Form 508. The section specifies that categorically eligible Assistance Units (AUs) do not need to verify certain information, such as resources and Social Security numbers, but does require gross income verification to determine benefit levels. Notable exceptions include conditions like having ineligible members (e.g., ineligible alien or student) that do not affect eligibility but exclude their inclusion in the AU. It cannot answer questions about the specific processing of strikers, which should be referred to Section 3240, or seasonal farmworkers, addressed in Section 3235.
3215: Section 3215 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines policies for residents of shelters for battered women and children, focusing on eligibility for SNAP benefits. Key policies include the ability for women and children to apply as a single assistance unit or separately and the criteria for dual participation if the abuser is part of another assistance unit. Only the resources and income of the resident and her children are counted, with joint resources deemed inaccessible. The shelter must be a publicly operated or nonprofit entity, provide proof of nonprofit status, maintain a resident list, and possibly obtain USDA authorization if engaging in wholesale food purchases. This section does not apply to individuals not residing in authorized shelters (see Section 3200 for general residency rules). Caseworkers can use this section to determine eligibility and procedures for residents but should refer elsewhere for issues related to non-shelter dwellers or other types of assistance units.
3220: Section 3220 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the eligibility criteria and procedures for residents of drug and alcohol treatment centers seeking SNAP benefits. It specifies that an employee of the center must serve as the authorized representative for benefits application and receipt, and highlights the disqualification conditions from the Food and Nutrition Service (FNS) affecting the representative's status. The section differentiates between residents who apply as a single unit or with their children, excluding spouses, and sets out criteria for facility eligibility, such as being a licensed tax-exempt organization. Key procedures for both FNS-authorized and non-authorized retailers are detailed, along with the responsibilities for handling Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) cards. Notably, it disclaims involvement with non-resident participants of treatment programs, referring caseworkers to Section 3205 for those scenarios. Caseworkers will find guidance on assessing resident eligibility, authorized representative duties, and facility certification but should not expect coverage of non-resident treatment policies in this section.
3225: Section 3225 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses eligibility and requirements for residents of group living arrangements, focusing on disabled and blind individuals in personal care or supportive living homes. Key policy topics include the eligibility criteria for group living residences, the role of authorized representatives, specific steps for obtaining certification and maintaining nonprofit status, and the management of residents' SNAP benefits. Important details include the limit of serving between two to sixteen residents, and procedures for financial assessments such as calculating room/board supplements and personal allowances, with financial supplements managed through the Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Diseases (DBHDD). This section includes detailed steps for verifying eligibility and budgeting income and deductions, but does not cover cases where residents live in private households (see Section 3210) or corrections facilities (see Section 3215). Caseworker questions regarding verification processes, income calculations, and setting up electronic benefits transfers are addressed, while inquiries about policies for different living arragements are not.
3230: Section 3230 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual discusses the eligibility and verification criteria for residents of homeless shelters seeking SNAP benefits. It emphasizes that homeless shelter residents must adhere to the same eligibility rules as other Assistance Units (AU), with a focus on alternative mailing addresses and income/resource verification (refer to Section 3205 for homeless assistance unit policies). Procedures include accepting applications without a permanent address, authorizing benefits through the county department if needed, and assigning certification periods up to twelve months. Key decision points involve obtaining agreements from shelter managers for mail reception and ensuring verification of basic eligibility criteria. This section does not address policies related to Assistance Units with fixed addresses or specific living arrangements, which are covered in other sections. Caseworkers can use this section to understand steps for processing applications from homeless individuals, but questions about other housing scenarios should be directed elsewhere, specifically to Section 3205. This section also applies to transitional housing facilities (not just traditional homeless shelters), including situations where the facility provides some but not all meals. The 50% communal meal threshold (from §3205) determines individual AU status for residents here.
3235: Section 3235 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the policies and procedures related to seasonal farmworkers, both migrant and non-migrant. It outlines key criteria for identifying seasonal farmworker Assistance Units (AUs), including characteristics like engagement in seasonal agricultural work and temporary employment patterns. Important considerations include the treatment of destitute AUs, expedited application processing, income calculation from terminated and new sources, and specific exemptions for work registration and vehicle valuation. Thresholds such as liquid resources not exceeding $100 and income limits determine eligibility for certain benefits. Notably, scenarios involving permanent farmworkers are not covered here and may need to refer to section numbers outside of 3235. This section is intended to assist caseworkers in determining eligibility and processing applications for seasonal farmworker AUs but does not address broader agricultural employment issues outside the context of SNAP.
3240: Section 3240 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the eligibility criteria for Assistance Units (AUs) involving strikers. It specifies that AUs with strikers are eligible for SNAP benefits if they were entitled or could have been entitled to benefits the day before the strike began, and they must comply with standard work registration requirements. However, ongoing AUs cannot receive an increased allotment due to income decreases caused by a strike. Importantly, individuals not considered strikers include those affected by lockouts, unable to work due to striking employees, or those who have been laid off or replaced. The section provides a procedure chart, Chart 3240.1, for determining SNAP eligibility and benefit levels for AUs with strikers. This section clarifies that employees exempt from work registration requirements, such as caretakers of young children (e.g., Section 3200), are addressed here only if they are connected to pre-strike requirements. Caseworkers should reference this section for eligibility assessments involving strikes but must look elsewhere for unrelated employment issues or exemptions not linked to pre-strike criteria.
3245: This section of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses eligibility criteria for students, including exemptions such as age, physical or mental unfitness, work-study participation, employment requirements, and child care responsibilities (Section 3245). It outlines rules for recognizing institutions of higher education and differentiates between eligible and ineligible courses. It highlights that a majority meal provision by an institution renders the student ineligible for SNAP benefits. The section specifies that the enrollment status begins on the first day of the school term and ends when a student graduates or intends not to register for the next term. It includes a list of educational income sources excluded from SNAP budgets, such as Pell Grants and Federal Work Study Programs. Caseworkers should reference this section for processing student eligibility but should look to Section 3420 for policies regarding educational income reporting. Form 875 is highlighted as a tool for verifying eligibility related to work-study participation.
3300: Section 3300 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the non-financial eligibility criteria necessary for an Assistance Unit (AU) member to receive SNAP benefits. Key policy topics include the need for cooperation with eligibility investigations, compliance with laws, avoidance of intentional program violations, and meeting requirements related to citizenship or alien status, enumeration, identity, residency, and food stamp (FS) work requirements. This section does not encompass financial eligibility criteria, which are found in Section 3400. Additionally, it does not address detailed procedures for handling intentional program violations, which are detailed in Section 3700. Caseworkers can refer to this section for clarity on non-financial eligibility prerequisites and criteria assessment, but it will not provide guidance on processing financial eligibility limits or specific violation penalties.
3305: Section 3305 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the requirements for Assistance Units (AUs) to cooperate with eligibility investigations, specifically by entities like Quality Control (QC) and the Office of Inspector General (OIG). AUs must comply with QC reviews, and failure to do so results in termination of eligibility, with a specified period of ineligibility communicated through written notice. However, cooperation with OIG investigations of past eligibility is not mandatory, and non-cooperation does not immediately impact current benefits unless current eligibility is questioned. This section includes critical actions and decision points regarding QC cooperation and the implications of non-compliance, indicating specific actions for caseworkers to initiate or delay case closure based on AU cooperation levels. The section does not cover scenarios related to eligibility determination processes detailed in Section 3300. Caseworkers will find clarity on handling non-compliance with QC processes but will not find directives for situations involving mandatory OIG investigation cooperation.
3310: Section 3310 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the eligibility criteria and disqualification procedures for individuals identified as lawbreakers, including those who have committed certain felonies, probation or parole violators, and fleeing felons. Key topics include the permanent disqualification of drug felons (with exceptions noted after legislative changes effective July 1, 2016), requirements for compliance with parole/probation terms, and the disqualification process for fleeing felons, which involves verifying fleeing status through a four-part test and coordinating with law enforcement responses within specific time limits. A critical formality is the "Determining Fleeing Felon Status Four-Part Test" and procedures for agency response times within 20 to 30 days. Disqualification conditions for minors, first offenders, and individuals non-compliant with parole conditions are also addressed. Notably, scenarios involving initial applications or recertifications are covered, yet this section does not address eligibility for IPV disqualified individuals or those under work sanctions, which are detailed in Section 3625. This section guides caseworkers on eligibility determinations, compliance verification, and handling notices related to disqualification but does not cover IPV or work sanction cases.
3315: Section 3315 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual covers the rules and procedures regarding Intentional Program Violations (IPVs), including the disqualification of individuals from SNAP benefits for committing IPVs. Key topics include the determination of disqualification periods based on offense frequency (12 months for first, 24 months for second, and permanent for third offenses), with exceptions based on court-ordered periods. Notable conditions that belong elsewhere include inquiries about IPV budgeting for disqualified individuals, which should refer to Section 3625. Questions this section answers include how to establish an IPV (via court conviction or administrative finding), time limits for imposing disqualifications, and the necessity of using forms like the Prosecuting Attorney’s Consent (PAC) Agreement. This section does not address calculations related to overpayments, which are found in Volume IV, Benefit Recovery. Charts such as 3315.1 outline SNAP penalties, and terminology like "Disqualified Recipient System (DRS)" and "Administrative Disqualification Hearing (ADH)" are crucial for caseworkers.
3320: Section 3320 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses Citizenship and Alien Status requirements for SNAP eligibility. This section outlines specific categories of individuals eligible for SNAP benefits, such as U.S. citizens, Non-Citizen U.S. Nationals, lawful permanent residents, and select non-citizens, outlining the criteria they must meet. It includes key forms for verification such as birth certificates, naturalization certificates, and specific USCIS documentation. Decision points include verifying citizenship or immigrant status, compliance with the Child Citizenship Act, and understanding the impacts of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act effective from July 4, 2025, which alters eligibility for certain alien groups. Charts 3320.1 and 3320.2 delineate eligible alien groups, while chart 3320.3 provides verification requirements for each status. Situations not covered here include budgeting for Assistance Units with ineligible aliens, found in Section 3635, and application processing procedures, found in Section 3105. This section cannot answer detailed budgeting questions for ineligible AUs or processing specifics, which are addressed elsewhere.
3325: Section 3325 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual covers the policy topics of enumeration requirements, specifically the need for individuals to provide a Social Security Number (SSN) to be included in the assistance unit (AU) for SNAP benefits. Key decision points include the conditions under which good cause for failure to obtain an SSN can be established, the actions required when multiple SSNs exist, and procedures for resolving discrepancies with the Social Security Administration (SSA). Important forms and time limits include a 10-day period for SSN provision, documentation requirements within the Document Imaging System (DIS), and the use of charts 3325.1 and 3325.2 for procedural steps. NOT HERE IF conditions include budgeting considerations for non-compliant individuals, which are covered in section 3620. This section can answer caseworker questions about the process and timelines for obtaining SSNs, establishing good cause, and steps to take when an AU member is not enumerated, but it cannot address budgeting or compliance beyond enumeration, which are detailed in other sections.
3335: Section 3335 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the verification of identity for Assistance Unit (AU) members receiving benefits. It specifies that AU members must reside in Georgia without a specific length of residency. Required documentation for verifying residency includes a Georgia Driver's License, mortgage statements, leases, utility receipts, school records, or any responsible reference's written statement; this list is illustrative, not exhaustive. For recertification, the AU’s statement of continued residency is accepted unless conflicting information is available. Section 3335 cannot answer questions related to county-specific application processes, which are located in Section 3105, or non-residency-related identity documentation, thus directing users to the relevant sections. This section aids caseworkers by outlining acceptable identity verification documents and the process for recertification residency confirmation.
3340: Section 3340 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses residency requirements for SNAP eligibility. It outlines the rules for establishing state residency, including acceptable proof and verification methods. Key terms include "intent to reside" and "temporary absence." Important details include acceptable verification documents and the timeframe for establishing residency. This section does not address non-residency-related eligibility criteria, such as income, which are covered in Sections 3330 (Income) and 3360 (Resources). Caseworkers can find guidance on verifying residency status but will not find information on processing residency for migrants or different state benefits.
3345: Section 3345 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual provides an overview of the SNAP Employment and Training (E&T) Work Requirement, focusing on legislative authority from the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996 and the Balanced Budget Act of 1997. It outlines the administrative structure and case management process, which includes assessing participant skills and developing Individual Employment Plans (IEPs) to promote self-sufficiency. The section does not include specific forms, thresholds, or time limits; however, it emphasizes case management tasks such as service coordination and performance monitoring. Notably, scenarios involving non-E&T work requirements or general SNAP eligibility fall under different sections such as 3320. This section answers caseworker questions about case management roles and E&T expectations but does not address issues related to initial SNAP eligibility or benefits calculation.
3350: Section 3350 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses Work Registration requirements, detailing policy topics such as registration, participation, and sanctions for non-compliance during the eligibility process. This section defines the criteria for exempt and mandatory registrants, including notable exemptions for students, caretakers, and individuals unfit for employment due to verified medical reasons. Key forms include Form 859, the SNAP Consolidated Work Requirements Notice. It also distinguishes between work registrants and ABAWDs (Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents), noting effective dates for age-related thresholds. Specific scenarios, such as expedited application processing, belong in separate sections like 3110. Caseworkers will find guidance on determining work registration status but should refer to sections like 3380 for compliance failures and 3355 for ABAWD-specific rules. Critically, this section governs reverification frequency for medical incapacity exemptions: temporary incapacity requires periodic medical statements, but permanent or long-term conditions unlikely to improve do NOT require repeated reverification — a one-time physician statement suffices. Questions about how often a medically exempt registrant must provide updated documentation belong here.
3355: Section 3355 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on the policies concerning Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs) and their eligibility for SNAP benefits. It outlines ABAWD work requirements, time limits, waivers, and discretionary exemptions. Key elements include a 36-month time limit with a three-month benefit limit unless work requirements are met, detailed verification processes, and forms such as Form 858 for Comparable Workfare. Specific terminology, such as "ABAWD Time Clock" and "countable months," is defined alongside decision points for exemptions and compliance actions. Caseworkers will find guidance on determining ABAWD eligibility, monitoring work hours, and handling cases of non-compliance. This section is not appropriate for questions regarding general work registration and exemptions as those belong in Section 3350.
3360: Section 3360 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the E&T Participation Requirement, focusing on policies for ABAWD Eligibility Tracking in time-limited counties. It outlines documentation requirements using the ABAWD Time Clock in the Gateway system or the Manual ABAWD Calendar Tracking Form 507 for accurately accounting each month of the 36-month period. It includes detailed ABAWD Tracking Calendar Values, such as sanctions, exemptions, and work registration statuses. The section also covers resource and income calculations for ineligible ABAWDs and outlines when resources are excluded or prorated, directing practitioners to relevant sections like Section 3210 and Section 3625 for further detail. Notably, it specifies when sanctions should continue if a registrant moves county lines. Caseworkers can utilize this section to understand participation requirements, employment services specialist responsibilities, and case closure conditions, but should refer to other sections, such as Section 3210 for categorically eligible assistance units and Section 3625 for income budgeting issues, if those topics are concerned. This section does not cover scenarios related to other forms of employment support or non-SNAP E&T programs.
3365: Section 3365 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual details the E&T Enrollment Process, focusing on participant requirements such as program orientation, employability assessments, an Individual Employment Plan, and enrollment in allowable work activities. It outlines specific decision points, such as entering a "negative program completion" for failure to complete job-related activities without good cause, and documents scenarios for "positive program completion." Key forms and terminology include the Gateway system for documenting assessments and updates to Individual Employment Plans. Time limits for Individual Employment Plan updates are flexible and can be conducted via phone. Notably, scenarios involving exemptions for the ABAWD work status are covered in a different section, likely section 3350. Caseworkers can find guidance on assessing participant work history, education needs, and job search efforts, but queries about exemptions and eligibility determinations belong elsewhere.
3370: Section 3370 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines specific policy topics related to Employment & Training (E&T) Participation Activities, with a focus on requirements for ABAWDs, time limits, participation thresholds, and allowable components within education, work, and non-education/non-work categories. Notably, individuals must begin participation by the first full calendar month after referral, with a maximum of 120 hours per month in any E&T component. Educational activities are limited to twenty-four months, and job search or readiness must be less than 50% of total education/training hours. Key terminology includes ABAWD, SNAP Works, and Participant Support Services, among others. This section contains charts detailing qualifying and non-qualifying components and guidelines for vocational training. It does not cover student criteria for food stamps, which is covered in Section 3350. Caseworkers can find detailed guidelines on participation requirements and satisfactory progress definitions here, but questions regarding food stamp eligibility for students should refer to the appropriate section.
3375: Section 3375 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses Work Support Services with a focus on transportation and incidental participant support services. It explicates rules regarding transportation assistance, including the provision of upfront payments ($25 for the first month), monthly reimbursements ($50 per month), and arranged services (up to $200 per month), with conditions detailed in UAS Budget Code 549. The section specifies that arranged transportation is not eligible for participant payments if services are purchased directly by DFCS. Incidental services like drug screens, physicals, and educational fees are outlined, contingent upon available funds, with UAS Codes indicating specific allowances and limitations. This section includes Chart 3375.1 for transportation services and Chart 3375.3 for incidentals but does not cover employment services beyond referrals or duplicate services managed by other initiatives. Caseworkers can resolve queries about eligibility for transportation and incidental support but need to refer to sections beyond 3375 for questions related to other services like Section 3390 for Job Retention or Section 3400 for Employment and Training Programs.
3380: Section 3380 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the "Failure to Comply with Work Requirements." It outlines the general work requirements mandatory for non-exempt household members to maintain eligibility for SNAP benefits, including registration for work, participation in state-required programs, and not voluntarily quitting or reducing work hours below 30 per week. It stipulates specific sanctions and penalties for non-compliance, such as eligibility ineligibility periods following first, second, and subsequent violations. Key forms include the SNAP Sanction/Penalty Notice Form 333, and critical decision points include determining good cause and determining compliance with TANF/ES requirements for sanctioned individuals. This section also distinguishes between causes for sanctions and the steps necessary for compliance, detailed in Chart 3380.1. The section does not address failures to perform other required actions, which are covered in Section 3385. Caseworker questions about lifting sanctions, determining good cause, and fair hearing procedures can be answered here, but inquiries specifically about non-work-related compliance actions should be directed to Section 3385.
3385: Section 3385 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the "Failure to Perform Required Action" policy, which ensures that SNAP benefits do not increase if an Assistance Unit's (AU) income decreases due to noncompliance with requirements in TANF or other means-tested programs. It outlines specific TANF requirements, such as SSN provision and parental responsibilities, which if violated, result in penalization but no SNAP benefit increase. The section emphasizes using the TANF benefit amount that would have been received without noncompliance and details procedural steps for managing TANF work requirement sanctions, including using Gateway for processing. The section includes Chart 3385.1 but does not apply to situations like TANF denial for non-required actions or caps from Family CAP provisions, directing to Section 3380 for E&T work requirement failures. Caseworkers can find guidance on handling TANF-related noncompliance but should refer to other sections for failure due to procedural tasks or conditions like SSI involvement.
3400: Section 3400 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual covers the financial eligibility criteria for SNAP benefits, focusing on resource and income limits for Assistance Units (AUs). Key policies include resource thresholds of $4,500 for AUs with at least one member aged 60 or older or disabled, reverting to $3,000 if the member is ineligible or sanctioned, and income limits based on federal poverty levels (130% for gross income and 100% for net income). It specifies that categorically eligible individuals, such as TANF or SSI recipients, have different resource considerations, and explains that non-liquid resources are excluded from the eligibility determination for these groups. Caseworkers can use this section to determine eligibility based on the countable resources and income of AUs, but they should refer to Section 3210 for categorical eligibility details. This section does not cover detailed allotment amounts, which are found in Appendix A, Financial Standards.
3405: Section 3405 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the treatment of resources in determining SNAP eligibility. It outlines specific policy topics such as the resource limits for Assistance Units (AUs), the classification and counting of liquid and non-liquid resources, and the criteria for resource accessibility and ownership. Key decision points include determining the resource limit applicable to an AU, identifying countable resources, and evaluating scenarios for resource transfer disqualifications, as detailed in charts like 3405.1. Noteworthy thresholds include a $4,500 resource limit for households with a member aged 60+ or disabled, and $3,000 for other households, along with timeframes for considering commingled resources and penalties for resource transfers. This section does not cover policies related to real property, which are found in Section 3415. Caseworkers can use this section to determine resource eligibility and the impact of joint ownership, but it does not address income-related questions, which are covered in Section 3420.
3415: Section 3415 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the treatment of real property in determining resource limits. It categorizes real property as homeplace, non-income producing, or income producing. The homeplace, including the home and contiguous land, is exempt from resource consideration and remains exempt even if temporarily unoccupied for specified reasons. The section provides guidelines on valuing real property, including the use of fair market value and indebtedness. Notable exceptions include property involved in a good faith effort to sell, property related to maintaining an excluded vehicle, and property declared unmarketable by a competent authority. This section does not address financial resources or liquid assets; refer to Section 3405 for verification of indebtedness and Section 3420 for income-related inquiries. Caseworkers will find guidance on how to categorize and assess real property but will not find instructions for unrelated resources such as vehicles or non-real property resources.
3420: Section 3420 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses income-related considerations for determining eligibility and benefit levels, with a focus on types of income, inclusions and exclusions, and verification methods. Key topics include differentiations between earned and unearned income, with specific treatment rules for various income sources such as adoption assistance, alimony, and military pay. Notable forms and tools for verification include pay stubs, award letters, and specific electronic platforms like Truv and SteadyIQ. Important charts include Chart 3420.2 detailing types of income and their SNAP treatment. The section also highlights "NOT HERE IF" conditions, such as categorical eligibility criteria, which refer to Section 3210. It helps caseworkers determine the countability of income, exceptions to income inclusion/exclusion, and the verification process but does not address non-income-related eligibility criteria, which may be found in other sections of the manual.
3425: Section 3425 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual provides detailed guidelines on the treatment of self-employment income for SNAP eligibility. It delineates rules regarding the calculation of gross self-employment income, including a 40% standard deduction for business expenses if at least one expense is incurred by the Assistance Unit (AU). Specific IRS forms for verifying various business structures like partnerships, corporations, S-corporations, and LLCs are listed, along with allowable and unallowable expenses. The section outlines the handling of income from capital gains, boarder income, rental property, and farm losses, with instructions on annualizing income and criteria for non-annualized scenarios. Important charts, such as Chart 3425.1 and 3425.2, provide a framework for calculating allowable expenses and computing non-annualized income. Caseworkers will find this section useful for determining income calculations, allowable deductions, and verification processes, but should refer to other sections like 3400 or 3420 for related income types that don't specifically pertain to self-employment income.
3430: Section 3430 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on the inclusion and treatment of military pay, such as housing and subsistence allowances, in determining eligibility for assistance. It emphasizes that military pay is considered earned income when the military member is part of the Assistance Unit (AU), while contributions from non-AU military members are unearned income. Verification of military income is required using the Leave and Earnings Statement (LES). The section includes specific treatment rules for different types of military pay, detailed in Chart 3430.1. It also provides deductions guidance, such as not allowing federal tax or insurance deductions, and potential child support deductions referable to Section 3616. Notably, combat pay received by military members due to deployment is excluded from income consideration. This section aids caseworkers in determining income treatment from military pay but does not address non-military income queries, directed elsewhere in the manual.
3500: Section 3500 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual provides an overview of the procedures and requirements related to computer matches for verifying applicant and recipient eligibility. It emphasizes the use of primary social security numbers (SSNs) to match with government agency files for verifying income, resources, and other critical eligibility information. The section outlines the purposes of computer matches, such as verifying eligibility and benefit amounts, and pursuing legal actions for improper benefit receipt. Access to computer match information is through the Gateway System's Interfaces module, requiring a valid user ID and password, with all activity monitored to prevent unlawful access. Notably, information related to UCB or TANF received from Interstate matches is regarded as verified. This section does not address specific error resolution (see Section 3600) or manual case reviews (see Section 3400). Caseworker questions this section can address include procedures for accessing computer matches and understanding their purpose, but it cannot provide guidance on specific case error corrections or manual verification procedures.
3505: Section 3505 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on the Income and Eligibility Verification System (IEVS) and its role in verifying applicant and recipient data through computer matches with various state and federal files. Key processes include addressing discrepancies within 45 days and documenting actions according to Georgia Gateway Documentation Standards. The policy outlines the use of specific files such as SSA Prisoner Verification and SSA Death Verification inquiries. Notable exclusions (NOT HERE IF conditions) include eligibility determinations for TANF, Medical Assistance, or DSNAP, which are addressed in separate sections like 3035 Verification. This section equips caseworkers with procedures for handling data matches, verification requirements, and documentation needs but does not provide guidance on eligibility criteria outside SNAP, which are covered in section 3035.
3510: Section 3510 covers the National Accuracy Clearinghouse (NAC), a computer-match system that identifies households receiving SNAP benefits in multiple states simultaneously. It covers NAC match alerts, the caseworker workflow for resolving duplicate-participation flags, required notices, and timelines for closing or continuing a case when a NAC match is confirmed or disputed. NOT HERE IF: the question is about expedited service processing timelines, the Standard of Promptness (SOP), or postponed verification — those belong in §3105 and §3110. NOT HERE IF: the question is about reopening, reactivating, or continuing a case after the postponed verification deadline has passed — that scenario belongs in §3105 via Chart 3105.3.
3515: Section 3515 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the Clearinghouse system, focusing on the policies regarding wage and benefit information matching for SNAP applicants and recipients. Key decision points include denying applications or closing cases if NAC notices are unaddressed and matches unresolved, especially concerning primary individuals and added individuals to the assistance unit. The section outlines the procedural use of Clearinghouse data at various points, such as at initial application, renewal, reopening, and interim changes, with specific attention to wage reporting and verification. Notably, UCB information is considered verified upon matching, and potential overpayments lead to fraud referrals if income exceeds 130% of the Gross Income Ceiling. It provides guidelines on addressing wage and employment data, but does not cover verification specifics found in Section 3035. This section can answer questions regarding eligibility impacts related to wage matches but not about detailed verification processes or non-wage related income issues.
3520: Section 3520 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on the Social Security Administration (SSA) Prisoner Verification Inquiry, detailing procedures for verifying if a member of a SNAP assistance unit (AU) is incarcerated. Key decision points include how to handle employment verification for SNAP applicants, the use of fraud referrals for unreported employment during SNAP benefit receipt, and how to process prisoner alerts generated by matching SSNs with incarcerated individuals for over 30 days. Relevant forms and tools include the VCL (Verification Checklist), the Prisoner Verification Inquiry charts (3520.1 and 3520.2), and alert/task IDs like 11011, 11012, and 11023. This section prescribes specific actions for different prisoner match scenarios, requiring documentation of confinement, release, and conviction details. It does not cover employment verification beyond 30 days prior to SNAP benefits (refer to Section 3035 for Verification). It helps caseworkers navigate prisoner verification tasks but does not address how to handle unrelated SNAP eligibility inquiries.
3525: Section 3525 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the verification process for deaths reported by the Social Security Administration (SSA) in relation to SNAP applicants and recipients. The section highlights the use of SSA computer matches to identify deceased individuals applying for or receiving benefits and outlines the generation of system tasks for caseworkers. Notably, SSA death matches are not verified upon receipt; caseworkers must contact the assistance unit (AU) and issue a verification checklist requesting proof of death, such as a death certificate or obituary. A key decision point involves removing a deceased AU member from the household at different stages: immediately upon intake, at the first month of renewal or periodic reporting, or after timely notice during interim changes. Conditions involving unresponsiveness or disputes over reported deaths refer to Section 3035 for verification. Additionally, SSA computer matches might contain errors, and potential fraud cases should be referred to the Office of Inspector General. Caseworkers should note that issues surrounding interim changes when the primary individual dies are detailed in Section 3715.
3530: Section 3530 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on Social Security Number (SSN) validation for AU members. It outlines procedures for verifying SSNs with the Social Security Administration (SSA), addressing discrepancies at the initial application and renewal, and correcting SSNs through a documented process involving communication with the empi.helpdesk@dhs.ga.gov. This section includes decision points such as annotation of SSNs with an FV (federally verified) code, as well as steps for changing a validated SSN and requesting a client ID correction. Key components include Chart 29 (CHART 3530.1 – SSN VALIDATION), and instructions for dealing with erroneous SSNs or client IDs. The section explicitly does not cover scenarios related to SSN issues unrelated to AU member discrepancies or verification errors initiated by the SSA; such issues are likely addressed in other sections not specified here. Caseworkers can find guidance on resolving SSN discrepancies and merging client IDs but may need to consult additional sections for broader SSA-related inquiries.
3600: Section 3600 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual provides an overview of the budgeting process for determining financial eligibility for Assistance Units (AUs). It includes the prospective budgeting method, which involves estimating monthly income and expenses to calculate eligibility and benefit levels. Key deductions include a 20% earned income deduction, standard deduction, and various expenses deductions such as medical and dependent care. Income tests are applied, requiring AUs to meet the Gross Income Ceiling (GIC) and Net Income Limit. Documentation must detail all income, expenses, and calculations. This section does not address exceptions that may involve complex income scenarios covered in Section 3700. Caseworkers can use this section to understand income calculations and deductions, but it does not cover deduction-specific calculations for self-employment, for which Section 3800 would be referenced.
3605: Section 3605 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on the rules and procedures related to Prospective Budgeting. It outlines how representative income and expenses are used to determine SNAP eligibility and benefit amounts, highlighting methods for calculating fluctuating versus stable incomes and expenses. Key conversion factors for different pay frequencies and the verification process, including primary sources like Truv and acceptable alternatives, are detailed. Important charts include CHART 3605.1 for minimum verification requirements and CHART 3605.2-3605.4 for determining monthly income and expenses. Notable exceptions are scenarios involving income from specific contracts, which should refer to section 3035 on Verification. This section is helpful for caseworkers addressing questions on determining representative incomes/expenses, applying conversion factors, and verifying income sources but does not cover rules for penalty assessments or fraud investigations, which are addressed in other sections.
3610: Section 3610 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on SNAP budgeting, specifically addressing how to calculate and determine financial eligibility and benefit amounts for Assistance Units (AUs). It outlines decision points for handling child support income and expenses, received and paid through the Division of Child Support Services (DCSS), and how to process TANF income. Key tools referenced include Chart 3605.2 for income determination, Chart 3605.3 for expenses, and Appendix A for financial standards. It defines the gross income ceiling (GIC) at 130% of the federal poverty level and the net income limit at 100%. The section also instructs on the SNAP budget process through a series of steps involving income deductions, such as standard, medical, dependent care, and shelter deductions, and the determination of benefits via the Basis of Issuance table. Although this section addresses income and budgeting, it does not cover eligibility specifics for ineligible students or detailed deductions for child support, which are respectively covered in sections 3205 and 3616. Caseworkers might refer to this section to understand budgeting and income calculations but would need other sections for eligibility nuances and specific deductions.
3611: Section 3611 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual provides an overview of the permitted deductions from an Assistance Unit’s (AU) income when assessing financial eligibility and benefit levels for SNAP. Specifically, it outlines the following allowable deductions: 20% earned income, standard, excess medical, dependent care, child support, excess shelter, and homeless shelter. It emphasizes that deductions are not permitted for expenses covered by reimbursements or vendor payments but are allowed for expenses paid with loaned money. It is important to note that an AU's intent or ability to pay is not considered when allowing deductions. This section refers caseworkers to sections 3620, 3625, and 3635 for policies regarding deductions when dealing with non-compliant AUs, disqualified individuals, ineligible aliens, or ABAWDs. Caseworkers will find answers here about which deductions can be applied and the conditions under which they apply, but it does not provide information about the specific enumeration requirements themselves, which are covered in different sections.
3612: Section 3612 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the Earned Income Deduction, permitting a 20% deduction from the total countable gross earned income for assistance units (AUs) with earned income. This deduction helps cover withholdings and work expenses but is forfeited if income is not reported in a timely manner (see Section 3650 for Failure to Report Earned Income Budgeting). The section emphasizes the importance of filing timely reports of earned income to maintain eligibility for the deduction. Caseworkers will find guidance on applying the 20% deduction, but should refer to other sections for topics like initial benefits calculations or eligibility determinations not related to income deductions. This section does not encompass situations dealing with unearned income, which are detailed in Section 3613.
3613: Section 3613 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the application of standard deductions for Assistance Units (AUs). It mandates the use of an appropriate standard deduction to be applied to the AU's total countable income, with adjustments made annually according to USDA FNS cost of living adjustments (COLA). Effective from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026, this section outlines the specific deduction values applicable for that period. Notably, this section does not cover scenarios related to earned income deductions, which are addressed separately in Section 3612. Caseworkers can reference this section to understand which standard deductions apply annually and how they should adjust for inflationary changes, but will need to consult related sections for details on other types of deductions or eligibility criteria.
3614: Section 3614 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the Excess Medical Deduction. Key topics covered include rules for applying standard and actual medical deductions, with thresholds of over $35 monthly for verification and over $196 for claiming actual expenses. It outlines specific forms of verification, such as pharmacy printouts and Form 840 for transportation logs. Important exclusions, like special diets and Schedule I controlled substances, are highlighted. Tables provide guidance on allowable medical expenses and budgeting one-time or recurring medical costs. This section informs caseworkers on eligibility for medical deductions and verification requirements. It specifically doesn't address policies related to recertification for SNAP benefits found in sections 3710 and 3715. Caseworkers can determine allowable medical deductions and exceptions but won’t find information on general SNAP eligibility or other non-medical deductions here.
3615: Section 3615 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the Dependent Care Deduction, detailing the allowable costs and verification processes for such expenses. This section outlines the conditions under which dependent care costs for children under 18 or incapacitated individuals can be deducted, emphasizing that all costs incurred or billed to the Assistance Unit (AU) are deductible, with exclusions for expenses paid under programs like Transitional Child Care or CAPS. It specifies that transportation costs, tied to a household vehicle used for dependent care, may be deducted at state mileage rates. Verification of expenses usually relies on client statements unless questioned, requiring additional evidence like receipts or statements from providers. Key exemptions include expenses paid to a household member providing care or costs identified solely as educational. Caseworkers can find guidance on allowable expenses but should refer to Section 3360 for Employment and Training-related queries and verify that documentation aligns with these specific verification protocols.
3616: Section 3616 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual details the Child Support Deduction policies, specifying the verification process for legal obligations and actual payments necessary for SNAP budgeting. Key topics include the types of documents accepted for verifying child support obligations, such as court orders, divorce documents, or administrative records, and the criteria for budgeting past due child support, which must not have been deducted in previous budgets. The section clarifies that alimony is not eligible as a child support deduction, and verification is required at initial application, recertification, interim changes, and periodic reporting, or when information is questionable. Caseworkers can find guidance on verifying current child support payments but should refer to Section 3710 for recertification-related queries and Section 3730 for periodic reporting. This section does not address alimony queries, which are not applicable under the child support deduction.
3617: Section 3617 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the criteria and guidelines for determining shelter and utility deductions for Assistance Units (AUs), including rules for shared housing and temporarily unoccupied residences. Key aspects include the necessity for third-party verification of shelter expenses effective July 1, 2024, and the eligibility criteria for the Heating/Cooling Standard Utility Allowance (H/C SUA) at $405 and the Limited Standard Utility Allowance (LSUA) at $358. Notable charts (3617.1, 3617.2, and 3617.3) provide details on allowable housing expenses and the conditions under which different utility standards apply. Decision points include verifying expenses for shared utility situations and handling payments between AUs. Understanding is not applicable for penalty payments or basic maintenance costs, which do not qualify as allowable expenses and are detailed in section 3035. Caseworkers can use this section to resolve questions about allowable housing deductions, eligibility for utility allowance standards, and verification processes, but it does not address non-shelter-related deductions or income evaluation questions.
3618: Section 3618 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on the Homeless Shelter Deduction, detailing eligibility criteria and application procedures for homeless households. It outlines that households claiming allowable shelter expenses at or below $199 are eligible for the homeless shelter deduction; those above may qualify for the excess shelter deduction or standard utility allowance but not both. Key rules include the necessity for third-party verification of shelter expenses and the mandatory documentation of criteria used to validate homelessness status. The section specifies scenarios where SUA allowances are applicable for shared living situations. Notably, matters related to shelter and utility deductions for housed individuals are addressed in Section 3617, not here. Caseworkers can utilize this section to determine eligibility requirements for the homeless shelter deduction but should refer to Section 3617 for guidance on excess shelter expenses and utility deductions unrelated to homelessness.
3620: Section 3620 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines procedures for budgeting an assistance unit (AU) containing individuals who fail to comply with enumeration requirements. Key policy topics covered include the exclusion of sanctioned individuals from the AU count for resource and income limits, and the prorating of sanctioned individuals' income and expenses among remaining AU members. The procedures detail steps for computing income and benefit levels, such as subtracting allowable income exclusions and dividing income among AU members. Notably, the section specifies that the full standard deduction is allowed and the H/C SUA or non-LSUA is never prorated. Caseworkers will find answers to questions on calculating benefit levels for AUs with enumeration-sanctioned individuals, but questions relating to separate policies, such as those dealing with other types of sanctions like work requirement failures (see Section 3400), should be referred to their respective sections. Forms, specific thresholds, and time limits are not prominent in this section.
3625: Section 3625 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the budgeting process for an Assistance Unit (AU) that includes individuals disqualified due to Intentional Program Violations (IPV), work sanctions, or lawbreaking activities. This section emphasizes the exclusion of such individuals from AU considerations when determining resource limits, income, and benefits, while their entire income remains countable toward the eligible members. The procedures include detailed steps for computing income, applying deductions, and issuing notifications regarding disqualification without requiring timely notice for IPV cases. Notably, scenarios involving Intentional Program Violations are referenced from Section 3315, Lawbreakers from Section 3310, and Work Requirements non-compliance from Section 3380. Caseworkers will find guidance on income computation, notification procedures, and disqualification implementation, but this section does not address eligibility determinations not related to IPV, work sanctions, or criminal activities.
3630: Section 3630 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the budgeting process for assistance units (AUs) with sponsored aliens. It details the rules on deeming a sponsor’s income and resources to the immigrant, with exceptions such as those without sponsors or those whose sponsor has not signed a legally binding affidavit of support (Form I-864 or I-864A post-December 19, 1997). The section emphasizes the exempted groups from deeming, including indigent aliens and situations like a sponsor living with the alien or passing away. It specifies verification processes with forms like INS Form G-845 and involves reporting indigent aliens to the U.S. Attorney General. Noteworthy is the exclusion of deeming for AU members referenced in Section 3635. The section answers questions about resource and income calculation, sponsor cooperation consequences, exceptions to deeming, and responsibilities regarding overpayments, but does not address budgeting for ineligible aliens or ABAWDs, covered instead in Section 3635.
3635: Section 3635 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the budgeting procedure for Assistance Units (AUs) containing ineligible aliens, non-applicants, or Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs). It provides detailed steps for calculating income exclusions, dividing countable income among all AU members, and applying deductions. Notable rules include prorating income and deductions while excluding the ineligible individual's share when determining benefit levels. Important terminology includes "pro rata share," "standard deduction," "H/C SUA," and "LSUA." The section specifies not to allow certain deductions if the ineligible individual is the sole eligible party for those benefits. It does not cover cases where the ineligible person is treated as an eligible member—the relevant guidelines for such scenarios are found in a different section. This section aids caseworkers in determining income deductions and benefit levels but does not address eligibility criteria or procedures for including ineligible individuals in AU size calculations.
3640: Section 3640 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on the budgeting procedures for contract employment. It outlines a step-by-step process for determining an individual's total gross monthly income by dividing annual gross income by twelve and adding it to other income, followed by applying standard income deductions and assigning a period of eligibility. Caseworkers should note that these procedures do not apply during expedited processing for applications filed during non-work or non-pay periods, when contract payments deviate from agreed terms, or when earnings are disrupted by labor disputes. This section doesn't specify forms, thresholds, or time limits, nor does it include charts or unique terminology. Additionally, any scenarios related to budgeting for non-contractual employment should consult Section 3650, while questions about expedited application processing should refer to Section 3700. Caseworkers will find answers here regarding budgeting contract income but not for handling irregular income situations outside a contract context.
3650: Section 3650 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the procedures and rules regarding the failure to report earned income timely. It specifies that the 20% earned income deduction is not applicable for income not reported within the required timeframe. Key decision points include understanding the threshold for gross income changes, which are to be reported if they exceed 130% of the applicable Federal Poverty Level. The section also sets a 10-day reporting period post-month-end, for income exceeding the Standard Reporting Requirement (SRR), and outlines the 10-14 day period for taking actions for SRR Assistance Units (AUs). This section does not cover scenarios related to interim changes, which are discussed in section 3715. Caseworkers can use this section to determine overpayment periods and apply the correct reporting requirements but should refer to other sections for changes not related to income reporting or budgeting.
3700: Section 3700 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on ongoing case management, which encompasses the activities from the approval of assistance units (AUs) continuing as long as they remain eligible.
