Key policy topics include the requirement for AUs to receive proper notification of any case action, cooperation with periodic eligibility reviews, and mandatory reporting of changes that could impact eligibility or benefit levels. It emphasizes timely processing of all reported changes and outlines the AUs' right to request hearings on case actions. Additionally, it addresses the recovery of overpayments as detailed in Volume IV, Benefit Recovery. Specific within this section are the rules around eligibility notifications and changes, but it does not address initial eligibility determinations (See Section 3100) or detailed procedures for benefit calculations, as those fall under different policies. Caseworkers can rely on this section to understand ongoing notification and reporting requirements but should refer elsewhere for benefit calculation queries.
3704: Section 3704 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the Transitional Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (TSNAP), focusing on eligibility criteria and processing guidelines for SNAP assistance units (AUs) transitioning from cash assistance due to employment-related changes. The section specifies that TSNAP benefits last for five months, with eligibility hinging on the closure of TANF or Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) due to new or increased earnings. It provides instructions on determining benefit amounts, reporting requirements, and end-of-transitional period procedures. The section also details conditions that disqualify AUs from TSNAP, such as failure to provide necessary information or non-compliance with TANF work requirements. Notably, cases are not eligible for TSNAP if the TANF closure is unrelated to earnings changes. This section answers caseworker questions on TSNAP eligibility, benefit calculation, and necessary notifications but does not cover regular SNAP procedures or issues unrelated to the transition from TANF/RCA, which are detailed in other sections.
3705: Section 3705 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the requirements for providing written notifications to Assistance Units (AUs) regarding decisions on applications and benefits. This includes notifications related to approvals, denials, changes in benefit levels, and sanctions. Key forms include Form 333, used for notifying AUs about sanctions or penalties. The section distinguishes between "adequate" and "timely" notices, specifying that timely notices require a 14-day waiting period before actions take effect, allowing AUs to request a fair hearing during this period. This section does not address issues related to hearings themselves, which are covered in Appendix B, Hearings. Caseworkers can find guidance on when and how to provide notifications but should refer to other sections for information on hearing procedures or unusual termination cases.
3710: Section 3710 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the policies and procedures regarding Recertifications (Renewals), including distinctions between timely, untimely, and late renewals. It specifies the key forms required, such as Form 297, Form 297A, Form 508, and Form 859, and highlights acceptable methods of electronic signatures. The section provides detailed timelines and processes for handling renewals, such as the Standard of Promptness (SOP) and specific decision points around the 15th and 30th days of the renewal period. Key charts include Chart 3710.1 for processing renewals. Caseworkers can refer to this section for guidance on renewal application processing, interview requirements, and eligibility criteria but should consult Section 3715 for Interim Changes and Section 3730 for Periodic Reporting policies. The section does not address the specifics of Senior SNAP, which can be found in Section 3725.
3715: Section 3715 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual specifically addresses the protocol for handling interim changes in the circumstances of the Assistance Unit (AU). Key topics include reporting requirements based on certification periods, as well as detailed procedures for acting on income changes, medical expenses, shelter costs, and changes identified via interfaces or alerts. Notable rules include the Simplified Reporting Requirements (SRR) and the 10-day time limit for the AU to provide verification once requested. Scenarios related to underpayments and overpayments belong in Section 3810. This section provides guidance on handling increases or decreases in benefits due to reported changes, verification processes, deadlines, and actions on unclear information. It helps caseworkers understand the specific actions needed when processing reported changes during the certification period, but does not cover initial application procedures or mass changes, which are discussed in other sections.
3720: Section 3720 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the reporting requirements for SNAP applicants and recipients. Key topics include the Simplified Reporting Requirements (SRR), which dictate that changes must be reported within 10 calendar days from the end of the month in which they occur. Specifics include reporting substantial winnings of $4500 or more and changes in income exceeding 130% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL). Form 339 and Form 846 are critical documents provided during application, recertification, or when necessary. Caseworkers should utilize this section to address reporting procedures and timely action on changes, but questions related to periodic reporting for Senior SNAP households should refer to Section 3730. The section also addresses actions required on various alerts and interfaces, including Social Security matches, but does not cover procedures for fleeing felons, which are detailed elsewhere.
3725: Section 3725 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual specifically addresses the Senior Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (Senior SNAP), which simplifies the application process for households with all members aged 66 or older (60 prior to February 2, 2026) with fixed, earned-income-free sources such as RSDI, SSI, and VA benefits. All Senior SNAP applications, initial and recertification, require specific verifications (e.g., identity, citizenship, income if not matched by state or federal sources) and follow a 36-month certification period with simplified reporting. Key forms include Form 298 and Form 508 for recertification, and applications can be submitted via mail or fax to a specified address. Situations that transition households to regular SNAP without reapplication are clarified under section 3730 for periodic reporting, and section 3035 for further verification points. This section addresses interview requirements, reporting obligations, and electronic signature acceptance; however, it does not cover detailed procedural charts or changes unrelated to Senior SNAP eligibility. Caseworkers will find answers regarding eligibility criteria, recertification processes, and handling of electronic signatures, but not for SNAP budgeting specifics or claims processing, which are handled by other sections or units.
3730: Section 3730 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on the requirements and procedures for periodic reporting. Key topics include the necessity for households to submit a periodic report to maintain benefits, the specific verification requirements for changes in household circumstances, and conditions under which expedited processing does not apply. The section specifies the use of forms such as Form 528 and Form 859, and details time limits for filing reports, typically by the 5th of the due month, with procedures for late submissions. Important decision points include determining whether verification is required and processing timelines dependent on the report meeting specific conditions. The section cites Chart 3035.1 for verification requirements and addresses potential incorrect scenarios that relate to but are distinct from this section, such as work registration status (refer to Section 3350) and Senior SNAP conversions (refer to Section 3725). This section assists caseworkers in addressing questions related to periodic report processing, verification requirements, and SNAP benefits continuity, but does not cover initial application, recertification procedures, or detailed work registration policy.
3800: Section 3800 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual provides an overview of the issuance process for SNAP benefits, detailing the methods and requirements for distributing benefits to eligible assistance units (AUs). Key topics include the authorization of benefits via Gateway and the mailing procedures for EBT cards. The section outlines specific conditions under which EBT cards may be mailed to different addresses, including residential, mailing, and Post Office Box addresses, with notable restrictions such as not mailing in care of another person. For homeless or seasonal farmworker AUs, alternative mailing addresses should be explored, and provisions are made for mailing EBT cards to county offices if necessary. This section does not cover details related to eligibility determination (see Section 3700). Caseworkers can use this section to understand the mailing and delivery procedures for EBT cards but should refer to other sections for eligibility and application processing guidelines.
3805: Section 3805 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual details the procedures and guidelines for managing Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) accounts. It addresses policy topics such as account setup, activation, replacement, manual issuance of benefits, voiding benefits, erroneous debits, and re-obligation. Key forms mentioned include EBT Form 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10, while notable time limits include the 9-month expungement period and 10-business-day resolution for erroneous debits. PIN selection and provision for card skimming and cloning incidents are explained. This section clarifies actions involving setup and maintenance of EBT accounts but excludes details on standard benefit determination or eligibility criteria, which are covered in Sections 3700 and 3900. Caseworker questions about routine benefit calculations and eligibility determinations should be directed to relevant eligibility sections, not 3805.
3810a: Section 3810a of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the issuance of SNAP benefits, including the rules and scheduling for both initial and ongoing monthly benefits. It outlines the use of electronic funds transfer (EFT) and the issuance of benefits via an EBT card with a PIN. Key topics include initial month issuance procedures, prorating initial month’s benefits using specific multiplication factors for each application date, and the schedule for posting ongoing benefits based on client ID numbers. The section specifies items that SNAP benefits can and cannot purchase, such as food intended for human consumption versus alcohol or tobacco. Noteworthy scenarios not covered here include manually issued benefits, which are found in Section 3805. This section can help caseworkers determine benefit issuance schedules and amounts but does not address manual issuance procedures or other non-EFT resolutions.
3810b: The Georgia SNAP Policy Manual, Section 3810b, focuses on the issuance of benefits, specifically restoration, food loss replacement, and supplemental benefits. It details conditions under which benefit restorations are authorized, such as agency errors or court orders, and sets a twelve-month limit for retroactive restorations. It outlines procedures for replacing food destroyed by disasters, including required documentation and a 10-day reporting window post-disaster. The section indicates that restorations are not applicable for initial allotments, disaster replacements, or expunged benefits. Forms like the "Food Loss Replacement Form (Form 841)" are mentioned, along with specified benefit availability dates based on client ID numbers. This section answers questions about benefit restoration processes and disaster-related food replacement but directs caseworkers elsewhere (e.g., 3610 SNAP Budgeting) for details on SNAP budgeting.
5459: Section 5459 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual details the Authorization for Release of Information, emphasizing the impermissibility of using unsigned, blank Form 5459 for any purpose. It specifies that information can only be released or obtained when the applicant/recipient (A/R) or personal representative (PR) clearly identifies which information should be handled. This section also outlines compliance with HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules, including administrative requirements such as the designation of a privacy officer, privacy and security training, and enforcement of sanctions for non-compliance. Key guidelines for safeguarding Protected Health Information (PHI) include restricted discussions, secure handling of records, and usage of secure containers for discarding PHI. Business Associate Agreements require notifying associates of compliance responsibilities. Note that issues pertaining to PHI data sharing security within internal electronic systems may belong elsewhere, potentially under sections specifically addressing digital records. This section answers questions regarding the proper completion and usage of Form 5459 and HIPAA compliance measures, but does not address technical IT security measures for electronic PHI storage.
5460: Section 5460 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the Notice of Privacy Practices effective December 2023, specifically in a Spanish language context. This section details the policy requirements for notifying applicants and recipients about the privacy of their personal information, including how it can be used and shared. Key forms include the Privacy Practices Acknowledgment Form, which must be completed and submitted. Notable thresholds include the time limits for acknowledging receipt of privacy practices. This section does not address eligibility criteria or benefits calculations, which are covered in Sections 3300 and 4900, respectively. Caseworkers can refer to this section to understand the protocols for informing clients about their privacy rights but should consult other sections for guidance on processing benefits applications or handling appeals.
5667: This segment of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines procedures for requesting a case review, detailing specific EBT control processes and community outreach services related to SNAP and TANF programs. It includes key forms such as the EBT Control Logs (EBT 2-7), TANF Community Outreach Services brochures, and a variety of forms addressing SNAP-specific processes like Verification Checklists and Applications for TANF, Food Stamps, or Medical Assistance. Important thresholds include gap budgeting for TANF recipients and the distinction between IV-D and non-IV-D child support cases. It does not cover civil rights complaint processes (see section 3030) or voter registration information (refer to * or Appendix F). This section addresses caseworkers' questions regarding the issuance of benefits, time limits for service procedures, and documentation requirements but does not address detailed civil rights cases or voter registration specifics.
